originality.rationale: The novel comparison concerns the distribution of the *actual signed vertex score* along a tilted-start simple walk on independently signed d-regular graphs, at consecutive odd/even times. The motivating paper proves score dominance only versus the starting time and computes a different one-step conditional-mean-bias distribution. Its higher-time local-limit theorems do not state paired marginal mixtures, a strict convex order and stochastic incomparability at equal means, the exact variance gap, or its return-probability asymptotic. The earlier multi-level degree-bias paper concerns degree instead of independent signed scores. Scoped semantic searches and statement-level comparisons revealed no equivalent or dominating theorem; priority is not externally certified.
residual_risks: Priority relative to unindexed work on random walk in independently marked tree scenery and convex order is not conclusively resolved.
The result concerns the limiting conditional time-marginals, not a pathwise convex-order coupling at finite graph size.
No uniform-in-time finite-n convergence or independent assessment is claimed.

value.rationale: The prior general theorem controls signed-score improvement versus the starting state, but explicitly leaves successor-time behavior unresolved. This exact distributional comparison shows adjacent times can have identical means and still differ by strict convex order and fail both directions of stochastic dominance, for every positive exponential tilt and every nondegenerate sign bias on the natural random-regular family. The explicit variance gap and decay law quantify a structural fluctuation oscillation rather than a narrow numerical exception.
